title: connection_lost for asyncpg now leaves idle connections open

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/10862
Originally posted by **chamini2** January 10, 2024 https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/commit/e70a0b0a0e52945e5b588b5cffec619a3f3e78a1 introduced a change where we would start seeing this error ``` Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/pool/base.py", line 377, in _close_connection self._dialect.do_terminate(connection) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/asyncpg.py", line 1109, in do_terminate dbapi_connection.terminate() File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/asyncpg.py", line 892, in terminate self.await_(self._connection.close(timeout=2)) File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/_concurrency_py3k.py", line 130, in await_only return current.driver.switch(awaitable) # type: ignore[no-any-return] ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/sqlalchemy/util/_concurrency_py3k.py", line 195, in greenlet_spawn value = await result ^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/asyncpg/connection.py", line 1467, in close await self._protocol.close(timeout) File "asyncpg/protocol/protocol.pyx", line 618, in close File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/asyncpg/connection.py", line 1584, in _cancel await connect_utils._cancel( File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/asyncpg/connect_utils.py", line 1040, in _cancel tr, pr = await _create_ssl_connection( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/asyncpg/connect_utils.py", line 752, in _create_ssl_connection do_ssl_upgrade = await pr.on_data ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ConnectionError: unexpected connection_lost() call ``` and that left connections open but idle, which would eventually make the PostgreSQL database reject connections becuase max was reached. I think maybe the `terminate` could be called for any exception, not just time out: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/e70a0b0a0e52945e5b588b5cffec619a3f3e78a1/lib/sqlalchemy/dialects/postgresql/asyncpg.py#L952-L958 ***** Stuff from issue creation, but did not have a reproducible example: sqlalchemy 2.0.25 PostgreSQL 14.9 Python 3.11 Linux
